To ensure the integrity of the additive manufacturing process, the required feedstock must meet stringent material specifications outlined by engineers, accompanied by vendor certification and rigorous material testing to verify compliance. Furthermore, material characterization testing is performed throughout the feedstock's life cycle during fabrication, guaranteeing that optimal processing parameters can be achieved to produce parts with full density. The development of the machine-agnostic process parameter and machine maintenance plan was made possible through collaborative efforts, published research in journals, and in-house investigations. By integrating these elements, a robust and reliable process can be established, ensuring the quality and performance of AM parts. 1.0 Design The design of an AM part is primarily driven by the specific application need, taking into account associated restrictions such as size and material, as well as limitations including performance behavior and lifespan. Once these parameters are defined, the geometry of the part can be designed. However, it is crucial to consult with AM operators at this stage to determine whether the design should incorporate supports or geometry alterations to facilitate fabrication and avoid potential build failures. The size of the part is also a critical consideration, as it may require different build volumes to produce a monolithic part or necessitate the incorporation of joining points throughout the part if it must be fabricated in sections and assembled later. As the design takes shape, it must undergo a series of rigorous reviews to ensure its viability. This involves assessing design limitations based on input from application engineers and AM operators, identifying and addressing any engineering anomalies, and finally, obtaining approval from a qualified engineer. This collaborative approach ensures that the design is optimized for AM, minimizing the risk of errors and maximizing the chances of successful fabrication. By considering the intricacies of the AM process and incorporating the expertise of various stakeholders, a robust and effective design can be achieved. 1.1 Feedstock Metal powder behavior and characteristics play a vital role in AM, as they directly impact the quality of the final parts. The powder serves as the fundamental basis for AM, and its properties must meet specific requirements to ensure optimal manufacturing capability and as-built part properties. Therefore, it is essential to carefully select and handle metal powders that meet the necessary standards. The manufacturing method of metal powder significantly influences its characteristics. Water atomization, although not widely used, can produce powders with higher oxygen concentrations and irregular morphologies due to the fast cooling and solidification rates.
